reason: The closure holds. I recounted every number from r7_gaps_out.json and they match. Under 20 um: g1 TP 1 / FP 137, g2 TP 2 / FP 149, g3 TP 2 / FP 172. Under 10 um: 2 TP / 63 FP. All TPs are in 6bba. There are 93 sandwich holes, 81 of them raw misses. The script's 7 um per-frame Hungarian matches the official max_distance of 7.0. The TP test (a GT path free of pred nodes, with linear interpolation within 7 um of each intermediate) is the right one for an interpolating bridge. The verdict rests on the ceiling, not on the FP proxy: at most ~5 recoverable gaps (~12 edges against ~40k GT edges, <= ~+0.0003), which is below the 0.005 noise floor even at 100% precision. The FP proxy (a matched end with a GT successor, or a matched start with a GT predecessor) approximates the official both-endpoints rule, and pairs are counted non-exclusively rather than by LAP. That inflates FP, but the mutual-NN arm still gives 60 FP vs 2 TP under 10 um. Two caveats do not flip the verdict. (1) exp60 is in-sample for the detector and edge net, so hidden embryos may have more gaps. But the LB already shows that widening gap closing does not pay (gap radius 6.5 um gave LB -0.001; 2-frame gaps gave no gain), and x138's gap/gap2 stages already run on test. (2) Small correction: the unevaluable pairs under 10 um number 3,654 (457 + 1,354 + 1,843), not ~3.9k. Each one would still add interpolated nodes, and fewer nodes is a bonus in this metric. Side fact: x138's existing synthetic nodes rarely match GT (gap 58/5,647, gap2 29/2,968, readmitted 73/13,284), so more interpolation mostly adds node count. Feasibility: nothing is proposed, so there is nothing to gate. Any revival would need a new build, a dummy run and an LB probe before R8 (27 Sep 12:00 UTC) for a ceiling below noise, and the finals #37 + #38 are already fixed.
